findings.passage: This voter ID measure conflicts with state law. Not only is it a solution in search of a problem, laws like these are harmful to California voters, especially low-income, the elderly, people of color, those with disabilities, and young voters.
findings.note: Statement in her name in the Secretary of State news release announcing the suit against Huntington Beach's charter voter ID rule for city elections.

findings.passage: Voter ID requirements have historically been used to turn eligible voters away from exercising their right to vote,
findings.note: Second quoted sentence from the same news release. The release also says each person who registers must give identifying information under penalty of perjury, which officials check.

findings.motion: Lawsuit in Orange County challenging Huntington Beach charter amendment requiring voter ID at the polls in city elections (filed with the Attorney General)
findings.note: As Secretary of State she joined the Attorney General in suing to block the city's voter ID rule, saying state law bars local governments from imposing voter ID. The release says they warned the city by letter on 2023-09-28.

findings.passage: This ruling does not affect California’s upcoming general election, and to be clear, we do not have any intention to use this concerning database,
findings.note: Statement in her name on a U.S. Supreme Court ruling letting the federal SAVE database be expanded to check voter eligibility; she says California will not use it.
subjects: federal SAVE database for voter eligibility

findings.passage: California has robust state law requirements that only U.S. citizens can register to vote and that any non-eligible registrants are removed from the State’s voter rolls.
findings.note: Statement in her name responding to a federal Justice Department demand to review a list of people it believes are noncitizens on the rolls.

findings.passage: “But if you tell me everybody has to take their ID to the poll, Californians should be concerned because 90% of them don’t want to do that,” she said. “They want to vote by mail, and you would effectively eliminate vote by mail.”
findings.note: Her words in a KCRA Sacramento TV interview, quoted in a Los Angeles Times story republished on dnyuz.com dated 2026-10-02 (interview aired the same week; exact day not given). The story also says she said the state already requires ID for those who register to vote. Original TV interview not reviewed.

findings.passage: Weber, when asked about her statement this week, said in an email to The Times that Proposition 39 would “cause disruption” in the state’s mail-in voting system because it would require voters “to write private personal information on the ballots.”
findings.note: The Los Angeles Times (republished on dnyuz.com, dated 2026-10-02) reports her emailed explanation; the quoted words inside the sentence are hers. The story says the measure needs the last four digits of an ID number on mail ballots.

findings.passage: We fought that because that's within the control of the state of California. And we won. And so they can't demand that from us.
findings.note: From the page's transcript of a KPBS Midday Edition interview, on refusing a federal demand for the full state voter database (with Social Security numbers).

findings.passage: There is no fraud , no , no stealing of of elections.
findings.note: From the page's transcript of the same KPBS interview (transcript spacing kept as printed); speaking about court and study findings on the 2020 election.
